financing.summary: Dream Finders is very land-light: it does not report owned lots at all and controls its pipeline (52,574 lots at 2026-09-30) through finished-lot and land bank option contracts, and a related-party fund (DF Residential III, run by 49%-owned DF Capital) holds a right of first offer on its land bank deals. On 2026-10-20 it closed a $2.2B all-cash purchase of Beazer Homes, and Millrose Properties (Kennedy Lewis) financed about $1.07B of it: roughly $580M to land-bank about 7,000 Beazer homesites and $500M of 12% Series B preferred. Corporate funding is a Bank of America-led unsecured revolver (about $1.7B of commitments, $1.2B drawn before the deal), $600M of its own notes due 2028 and 2030, and $650M of assumed Beazer notes due 2031 and 2032 now being exchanged into Dream Finders paper. Leverage is the constraint (48.1% net homebuilding debt to net capitalization before Beazer, with $675M of 12% preferred on top) and management calls deleveraging a key priority; for a competing land banker the openings are Beazer's remaining owned land and deals outside DF Residential III's criteria, but Millrose now sits in both the land and the capital structure.
financing.land_strategy: Land-light. The company calls it an 'asset-light lot acquisition strategy': it generally avoids owning land under development and buys finished lots just in time through finished lot option contracts and land bank option contracts, with deposits averaging about 10% of the land price and option fees paid on the land banker's outstanding capital. No numeric target is stated. The 2026-08 merger presentation showed the combined Dream Finders plus Beazer position as 78% optioned and 22% owned.

lots.source_title: Dream Finders Homes Q3 2026 earnings release (Exhibit 99.1 to 2026-10-29 8-K)
lots.note: Dream Finders reports only a 'controlled lot pipeline' (lots under finished lot and land bank option contracts); owned lot counts are not disclosed in its 10-K, 10-Q or earnings release, so total, owned and percent optioned are left blank. Standalone and pre-Beazer. Down from 63,121 at 2025-12-31 (Southeast 23,616; Mid-Atlantic 23,517; Midwest 15,988) and 63,509 at 2026-06-30; management said it is terminating option deals that miss return thresholds and expects abandonment charges in Q4 2026. Against 2026 guidance of about 9,250 closings the pipeline is roughly 5.7 years (computed, not stated). Beazer adds 24,489 controlled lots (2026-06-30; 60.0% of its 23,083 active lots optioned). The merger presentation put the combined position at about 87,944 lots, 78% optioned and 22% owned.

ma.description: All-cash merger at $33.50 per share, about $878.4M of equity consideration and about $2.2B enterprise value; Beazer is now a wholly owned subsidiary and delisted. Began as private approaches from 2026-02-05, went public and hostile on 2026-05-11 at $25.75, raised to $32.00 on 2026-07-08, and signed at $33.50 on 2026-08-06. Funded by $675M of Series B preferred, a $572.1M Millrose land bank facility, revolver borrowings and cash.
ma.map_impact: Beazer stops being a separate builder: fold its row under Dream Finders. Combined company is about 12,800 CY2025 closings and $6.6B revenue (sixth-largest listed US builder by revenue, per DFH), about 520 communities in 26 markets, adding California, Nevada, Indiana and Delaware and deepening Maryland, Texas, Florida, the Carolinas, Georgia and Arizona. Beazer's nine directors (including Allan Merrill) resigned and were replaced by DFH's board; Beazer's officers stayed in place at closing; the integrated reporting structure for its land and division leaders has not been published. Beazer's Atlanta treasury relationships (JPMorgan revolver, 2029 notes) are gone; about 7,000 Beazer homesites moved to Millrose, and DFH has flagged option terminations and abandonment charges in Q4 2026.
ma.source_title: Dream Finders Homes Form 8-K (completion of Beazer acquisition)
ma.note: Combined figures from the 2026-08-07 merger presentation and 2026-10-20 closing release. Whether the Beazer brand continues is not stated; DFH plans to move Beazer communities to Dream Finders floor plans. DFH targets more than $100M of annual cost synergies and a return to pre-deal leverage in 18 to 24 months.
